bio: I am an undergraduate student of psychology at Ashoka University, with minors in biology and philosophy. The breadth of that training — biological mechanisms, philosophical argument, and psychological measurement — shapes how I approach research questions.

I am interested in cognitive processes such as attention and inhibitory control, and in clinical questions around emotional processing, childhood experiences, and mental health. Much of my work concerns how early experiences are carried forward into the way people attend to, interpret, and respond to emotional material.

Methodologically, I work with behavioral experimentation — reaction-time paradigms such as Go/No-Go tasks built in PsychoPy — alongside questionnaire research and quantitative analysis. I care about doing this work carefully: clear design, appropriate measures, and analysis that the data can actually support.
I hope to continue this line of work in graduate study, with an emphasis on [your intended focus].

goals: My current work examines how childhood emotional experiences relate to inhibitory control in emerging adults. In the longer term I want to keep working at the intersection of cognitive and clinical psychology, where experimental methods can be brought to bear on questions about mental health.
